title: steps/subagentStart payload
description: Fires when a parent agent spawns a subagent in-process — i.e., delegation that does NOT cross an A2A boundary. A2A-mediated delegation flows through steps/agentTrigger with trigger_type='a2a_inbound' on the subagent's side; subagentStart is for the same-runtime case. The audit chain must record whether the subagent inherits the parent's Intent.parsed, gets a derived intent, or starts fresh, and every spawn carries the subagent_intent a Guardian checks. A Guardian MUST deny a spawn whose subagent_intent grants capabilities outside the parent's Intent.parsed when intent_derivation is 'inherit_full', 'inherit_subset' or 'derived_from_parent', where the parent's Intent.parsed is the one the Guardian holds for parent_session_id, never one the payload supplies. A Guardian MUST deny a spawn whose subagent_session_id equals parent_session_id or the metadata.session_id of the envelope, or names a session it already knows; JSON Schema cannot compare two members, so this one is not a schema rule. The subagent's SessionContext starts from the parent's provenance and IFC labels, not empty (see parent_provenance_summary). Sessions are per-subagent: each subagent gets its own session_id and SessionContext; the parent–child relation is captured here.

subagent_session_id.description: Fresh session identifier for the spawned subagent. MUST differ from parent_session_id and from the envelope's metadata.session_id, which is the parent's session; a Guardian MUST deny a spawn where it does not, because a child that reuses the parent's id writes into the parent's chain and state. The subagent's own steps/* hooks will carry this id in their envelope metadata.session_id.

parent_session_id.description: Session id of the parent. Lets cross-session policies and audit replay reconstruct the spawn relationship.

parent_step_id.description: step_id of the parent's hook that triggered the spawn (typically a steps/toolCallRequest for a delegation tool, or a steps/agentResponse that the framework interpreted as a spawn directive).

parent_intent_id.description: provenance_id of the parent's Intent, that is the parent's Intent.parser_provenance.provenance_id, from which a derived intent descends. REQUIRED when intent_derivation is 'derived_from_parent', where subagent_intent.parser_provenance.derived_from MUST include it. Both are provenance_ids, so the rule compares like with like; parent_step_id is a step_id and is not a member of that identifier space.

parent_provenance_summary.description: Session-level provenance summary of the parent's context at the spawn. OPTIONAL on the wire. The subagent's SessionContext MUST start from the parent's provenance and IFC labels for 'inherit_full', 'inherit_subset' and 'derived_from_parent', and SHOULD for 'fresh'. A Guardian seeds the child from its own record of parent_session_id and treats this member as a floor: it MUST NOT seed the child with less than its own record, so a sender cannot launder a parent's untrusted or secret context by omitting or understating it.

intent_derivation.description: How the subagent's Intent.parsed relates to the parent's. 'inherit_full' = identical capability set (subagent_intent.parsed MUST equal the parent's parsed). 'inherit_subset' = strict subset (subagent_intent.parsed MUST be a subset of the parent's parsed). 'derived_from_parent' = the parent emitted a parsed delegation directive that the framework's intent parser turned into the subagent's intent (parent_intent_id is REQUIRED and subagent_intent.parser_provenance.derived_from MUST include it; subagent_intent.parsed MUST be a subset of the parent's parsed unless a Guardian policy explicitly admits more). 'fresh' = the subagent has its own user-derived Intent (subagent_intent.parser_provenance.origin MUST be 'user_input'; a spawn whose intent was generated by the agent is not 'fresh'). A Guardian MUST deny the first three when subagent_intent.parsed is outside the ceiling, and MUST resolve 'fresh' under its own policy, since no parent capability bounds it.

subagent_intent.description: The Intent that will govern the subagent. Same shape as the Intent in agent-trigger.json. REQUIRED on every spawn, with parsed and parser_provenance, so a Guardian always has the capability set it is asked to check. For 'inherit_full' it restates the parent's parsed; for the other derivations see intent_derivation.

subagent_descriptor.description: Optional descriptor of the subagent itself — its agent_id, model, framework version, etc. SHOULD be populated when the subagent is a distinct named component the deployment can identify (e.g., a research subagent, a coding subagent).
